question_text: What must you do if you notice signs of fatigue when driving on open stretches of road at night (heavy eyelids, feeling chilly, sudden frights etc.)?

options.text: Interrupt your journey for an adequate break
Switch on the radio and proceed

correct_answers.text: Interrupt your journey for an adequate break

comment: You can only avoid signs of fatigue if you take sufficiently long breaks in time. Do not turn on the radio to stay awake, as there is a risk it will distract you further. If you already feel the first symptoms of fatigue, find a place where you can take a longer break as soon as possible.

question_text: How can fatigue be prevented on a long journey?

options.text: By well-timed and sufficient stops for rests
Gymnastic exercises during stops
Drink coffee and make no stops

correct_answers.text: By well-timed and sufficient stops for rests
Gymnastic exercises during stops

comment: Timely breaks prevent overfatigue. Gymnastic exercises during the break pep up the circulation and are good for the joints. Coffee has only a short-term mobilizing effect, which can then quickly turn into the opposite. That means you could fall asleep without warning.

question_text:
What is the potential risk when using driver assistance systems?
The vehicle driver may

options.text: - have false expectations of the systems
- pay too little attention to the traffic around him
- neglect his own personal responsibility

correct_answers.text: - have false expectations of the systems
- pay too little attention to the traffic around him
- neglect his own personal responsibility

comment: The car driver may have too high expectations of the advanced driver-assistance system. This may result in the car driver neglecting his or her own responsibility and paying too little attention to the traffic. Even when using advanced driver-assistance systems, the responsibility for safe driving remains with the driver.

question_text: What is the risk if you become distracted while using electronic devices when driving?

options.text: I may deviate from my lane
I may fail to notice road traffic signs
My stopping distance may be reduced

correct_answers.text: I may deviate from my lane
I may fail to notice road traffic signs

comment: Using electronic devices while driving can cause you to miss traffic signs and wander off your lane (concentration distracted).

question_text:
What frequently causes younger drivers to have “disco accidents”?
The drivers fail to notice that they

options.text: - are over-tired
- are physically exhausted
- are not fit to drive

correct_answers.text: - are over-tired
- are physically exhausted
- are not fit to drive

comment: All three are correct. The so-called disco accidents are caused by overtiredness, by physical exhaustion and by being unfit to drive.

question_text: What is the right thing to do if you sense signs of fatigue during a night-time journey?

options.text: I interrupt the journey to take an adequate break
I allow a co-driver to drive, if possible
I decide against taking a break, and fight the tiredness

correct_answers.text: I interrupt the journey to take an adequate break
I allow a co-driver to drive, if possible

comment: As soon as you feel tired, you should take a break immediately. The risk of falling asleep increases with every second. If possible, you can let your passenger drive if they have the driving licence.

question_text: What can diminish alertness in road traffic?

options.text: Strong emotions (e.g. delight, annoyance, impatience)
Animated conversation
Engrossing programs on the car radio

correct_answers.text: Strong emotions (e.g. delight, annoyance, impatience)
Animated conversation
Engrossing programs on the car radio

comment: All external stimuli such as joy, anger, interesting things on the radio and lively conversations can negatively affect the attention while driving, as they can be distracting.

question_text: What strongly distracts you while you are driving?

options.text: Telephoning
Lighting a cigarette
Nagging children on the backseats

correct_answers.text: Telephoning
Lighting a cigarette
Nagging children on the backseats

comment: Telephoning while driving is only allowed via a hands-free system. Even then it is still a distraction. The lighting of a cigarette is considered a strong distraction, as it directs the view from the roadway to the cigarette. Whining children and passengers can be very distracting, if necessary, take a pause.

question_text:
When should you interrupt your journey?
When I

options.text: - want to pick an item that has fallen down in my vehicle
- notice that the concentration is decreasing
- want to activate the cruise control system

correct_answers.text: - want to pick an item that has fallen down in my vehicle
- notice that the concentration is decreasing

comment:
Especially on longer trips, it can always happen that concentration subsides. If you notice that your concentration wanes noticeably, you should definitely take a break.
You should also stop if you want to cancel an object that has fallen into the vehicle. By searching and lifting an object, you can distract yourself very much. Therefore, you can endanger yourself and other road users.
